title: Grammar: Advanced Reporting Verbs in Professional and Academic Writing
grammarTip:
Глаголы сообщения в академическом и деловом письме:

Для цитирования источников:
argues/maintains/claims → спорное утверждение
states/asserts/emphasises → прямое утверждение
suggests/implies/indicates → косвенное значение
concludes/finds/demonstrates → вывод из исследования

Для описания чужих действий:
acknowledges · highlights · notes · points out · observes · proposes

💡 Выбор глагола меняет тон:
"Smith CLAIMS..." (я не обязательно согласен)
"Smith DEMONSTRATES..." (доказал убедительно)
"Smith ARGUES..." (его позиция, открытая для дискуссии)

Проверь: какой глагол лучше всего описывает отношение автора к информации?

grammarTable.subject: Neutral reporting
grammarTable.example: "The report stated that recruitment costs had increased by 15%."

grammarTable.subject: Strong assertion
grammarTable.example: "She argued that the hiring process was fundamentally flawed."

grammarTable.subject: Acknowledging/conceding
grammarTable.example: "The manager acknowledged that the team was understaffed."

grammarTable.subject: Questioning/challenging
grammarTable.example: "The union disputed the company's claims about working conditions."

grammarTable.subject: Showing hesitation
grammarTable.verb: hesitated, seemed reluctant to, was unwilling to
grammarTable.example: "She seemed reluctant to commit to a specific timeline."

grammarExtra.title: Choosing the Right Reporting Verb: Precision Matters

rows.form: "said" vs "argued": argue implies a reasoned case, not just speech
rows.example: "He said the policy was unfair." vs "He argued that the policy violated workers' rights."

rows.form: "admitted" vs "acknowledged": admit = reluctantly; acknowledge = more neutral
rows.example: "He admitted making errors." (reluctant) vs "She acknowledged the complexity of the issue."

rows.form: "claimed" vs "stated": claim implies the statement may be doubtful
rows.example: "She claimed to have ten years' experience." (may not be true) vs "She stated her experience clearly."

rows.form: "proposed" vs "suggested": propose = formal plan; suggest = informal idea
rows.example: "The board proposed a merger." vs "A colleague suggested working more flexibly."

grammarExtra.title: Tense Changes in Reported Speech with Reporting Verbs

rows.form: Direct: "I will resign." → Reported: She threatened to resign.
rows.example: "The employee threatened to resign if conditions did not improve."

rows.form: Direct: "I took the file." → Reported: He admitted taking the file.
rows.example: "He admitted taking the confidential file from the office."

rows.form: Direct: "Please update your profile." → Reported: She reminded him to update his profile.
rows.example: "She reminded him to update his professional profile before the networking event."

rows.form: That-clause: tense backshift applies
rows.example: "He said the interview had gone well." (was → had been)

grammarExtra.title: Academic and Professional Vocabulary for Reporting

rows.form: emphasise, highlight, underline
rows.example: "The report emphasised the need for better training." (draw attention to)

rows.form: contradict, dispute, question
rows.example: "The data contradicted the manager's claims." (show to be wrong)

rows.form: conclude, determine, find
rows.example: "The study concluded that flexible working improved productivity."

rows.form: urge, call for, press for
rows.example: "The union urged the company to improve safety standards."

rows.form: It is argued that + clause
rows.example: "It is argued that remote work increases productivity for knowledge workers."

rows.form: It has been suggested that + clause
rows.example: "It has been suggested that the recruitment process should be reformed."

rows.form: It is widely believed / accepted that
rows.example: "It is widely accepted that job satisfaction depends on more than salary."

rows.form: The author / report / study + verb + that
rows.example: "The study found that autonomy was the strongest predictor of engagement."

grammarExtra.title: Stance and Attitude in Professional Communication

rows.form: Verbs that signal agreement
rows.example: agree, concur, confirm, accept, acknowledge

rows.form: Verbs that signal disagreement
rows.example: dispute, deny, reject, challenge, contradict, question

rows.form: Verbs that signal uncertainty
rows.example: wonder, speculate, question, be uncertain whether

rows.form: Verbs that signal obligation
rows.example: urge, insist on, require, expect, demand

exercises.instruction: Choose the most precise reporting verb.
exercises.text: "The research ___ that flexible working leads to higher employee retention." (found through study)
exercises.hint: "Found" is used when research/study produces a result

exercises.instruction: Which reporting verb implies the statement may be untrue?
exercises.text: "She ___ to have five years of relevant experience."
exercises.hint: "Claimed" implies the speaker may be doubtful

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct formal passive reporting structure.
exercises.text: "___ widely ___ that job satisfaction depends on autonomy and purpose." (it is accepted)
exercises.hint: "It is widely accepted that" = formal passive reporting

exercises.instruction: Choose the verb that shows a strong, reasoned position.
exercises.text: "He ___ that the current recruitment process was discriminatory."
exercises.hint: "Argued" = making a reasoned case, stronger than "said"

exercises.text: "She ___ (acknowledge) that the team was understaffed and promised to address the issue."
exercises.hint: "Acknowledge" = admit more neutrally, often of a problem

exercises.instruction: Choose the verb that signals disagreement.
exercises.text: "The union ___ the company's claims that wages had increased fairly."

exercises.instruction: Complete with a formal passive reporting phrase.
exercises.text: "___ been ___ that remote work should be made a legal right for eligible workers." (suggestion)
exercises.hint: "It has been suggested that" = formal passive reporting

exercises.text: "The CEO ___ the team to find a solution before the board meeting." (strong encouragement, almost demand)
exercises.hint: "Urge" = press strongly, more forceful than "suggest" or "recommend"

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct reporting verb + pattern.
exercises.text: "She ___ (maintain) that the decision had been made without proper consultation."
exercises.hint: "Maintain" = firmly hold to a position (strong assertion verb)

exercises.instruction: Which phrase is most appropriate for formal academic reporting?
exercises.text: "The study found that flexible working increased productivity."
opts: The study was like productivity increased.
The study told that productivity increased.
The study concluded that flexible working improved productivity.
The study said how productivity increased.
exercises.correct: The study concluded that flexible working improved productivity.
exercises.hint: "Concluded" = formal verb for reporting research outcomes

exercises.instruction: Replace "said" with a more precise verb.
exercises.text: "The lawyer ___ (deny formally) that her client had any knowledge of the fraud."
exercises.hint: "Deny + gerund or that-clause" — formal rejection of an accusation

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct passive reporting structure.
opts: It argued that the system was flawed.
It is argued that the system is flawed.
It argued the system was flawed.
It has been argued the system was flawed.
exercises.correct: It is argued that the system is flawed.
exercises.hint: "It is argued that" = formal passive reporting of a position

exercises.instruction: Complete with the best reporting verb.
exercises.text: "The consultant ___ restructuring the team to improve efficiency." (put forward a formal plan)
exercises.hint: "Propose" = put forward a formal plan (more specific than "suggest")

exercises.instruction: Which pair correctly contrasts two reporting verbs?
exercises.hint: "Argued" = making a case; "mentioned" = simply referred to

exercises.instruction: Complete with the correct form for formal reporting.
exercises.text: "___ ___ that the new performance management system has improved employee satisfaction." (researchers found)
exercises.correct: Research / suggests / has found (any formal reporting phrase)
exercises.hint: "Research suggests / has found that" — common academic pattern

exercises.instruction: Which is the most formal and precise report of this statement?
exercises.text: "'You must improve or leave,' he said to the employee."
opts: He told the employee to improve or leave.
He said the employee should improve.
He warned the employee to leave.
He mentioned improving to the employee.
exercises.correct: He told the employee to improve or leave.
exercises.hint: "Tell + object + to-infinitive" is the most accurate report

questions.text: "The study ___ that autonomous workers report higher job satisfaction." (research result)
"___ widely ___ that passion tends to follow mastery, not precede it." (formal passive)
questions.hint: "It is widely believed that" — formal passive reporting

questions.text: "She ___ that the company's recruitment process was biased." (making a strong, reasoned case)
"The HR director ___ that the pay gap was smaller than reported." (questioning the truth of a claim)
questions.hint: "Disputed" = challenged, disagreed with the truth of

questions.text: "The union leader ___ management to address the health and safety concerns immediately." (pressed strongly)
"Claimed" implies the statement is definitely true, unlike "stated."
questions.hint: "Claimed" implies the statement may be doubtful or unverified

questions.text: "The manager ___ that staff turnover had increased sharply — reluctantly accepting the evidence." (admit neutrally)
questions.hint: "Acknowledged" = admit more neutrally, without strong reluctance

questions.text: "___ been proposed that all employees should receive career coaching as part of onboarding."
questions.hint: "It has been proposed that" — formal passive, present perfect

questions.text: "She ___ (maintain) throughout the interview that her qualifications exceeded the requirements."
questions.hint: "Maintain" = firmly hold to a position throughout

questions.text: Which is most appropriate in a formal report?
opts: The manager said workers needed more training.
The manager went on about workers needing training.
The manager highlighted that workers required additional training.
The manager was talking about training workers.
questions.correct: The manager highlighted that workers required additional training.

questions.text: "___ ___ concluded that purpose, relationships, and autonomy are the strongest drivers of job satisfaction." (formal academic — use passive)
questions.hint: "It has been concluded that" OR "Research has concluded that"

questions.text: Which sentence signals that the person making the claim did so reluctantly?
opts: She argued that the system was unfair.
She denied that any errors had been made.
She acknowledged that the project was behind schedule.
questions.correct: She acknowledged that the project was behind schedule.
questions.hint: "Acknowledged" often implies admitting something somewhat unwilling
